name: Connecticut
tagline: From Litchfield Hills lakes to Connecticut River ferries and the Merritt Parkway's carved bridges.
intro: Connecticut's scenic roads loop around Litchfield Hills lakes and follow the Housatonic, cross the lower Connecticut River by ferry and swing bridge, run along the Sound at Branford and Old Saybrook, and pass village greens and stone-walled farms in the northeast. This chapter follows the State Scenic Roads list kept by the Connecticut Department of Transportation and its Scenic Roads Advisory Committee under regulations adopted in 1989. The state designates numbered pieces of state highway, often only a mile or two long and bounded by town lines and cross streets, so its 74 designations are gathered here into 43 drives by route and town; two of them, the Merritt Parkway and Route 169, are also National Scenic Byways.

members.name: Merritt Parkway
members.blurb: Route 15 runs 37 miles through Fairfield County woods from the New York line to the Housatonic, a 1930s parkway closed to trucks, where each original overpass wears its own Art Deco ornament.

members.name: Route 169
members.blurb: Route 169 follows the 1801 Norwich and Woodstock Turnpike north for 32 miles past stone walls, boulder-strewn fields and colonial meetinghouses, and through Pomfret Street, where two boarding schools share a two-mile historic district.

members.name: Routes 49 and 14A
members.blurb: Route 49 runs north from North Stonington through Pachaug State Forest, the largest in Connecticut, and climbs to hilltop farms in Sterling where stone walls fence in grazing cattle and tall corn.

members.name: US 7, Kent to Canaan
members.blurb: US 7 follows the Housatonic north for 28 miles, past the stepped cascades of Kent Falls and a fly-fishing-only stretch of river at Housatonic Meadows, crossing at Cornwall Bridge on its way to Canaan.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 4, Sharon to Cornwall Bridge
members.blurb: Four miles of Route 4 between Sharon and the Housatonic, on the line of the old Sharon and Cornwall Turnpike, ending at Cornwall Bridge, where the road joins US 7 to cross the river.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 41, Sharon and Salisbury
members.blurb: Route 41 crosses Connecticut's northwest corner from the New York line to Massachusetts, down Sharon's mile-long green, through Lakeville and out Under Mountain Road, where a trail climbs from the roadside to the Appalachian Trail.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US 44, Salisbury
members.blurb: Nine miles of US 44 across Salisbury on the old Salisbury and Canaan Turnpike, through Lakeville and Salisbury center, in hill country whose ironworks made gun barrels and railroad car wheels until about 1920.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lake Waramaug and New Preston
members.blurb: The roads around Lake Waramaug make a slow loop past cottages, boathouses and the state park on the northwest shore, then drop into New Preston, where the lake's outlet stream spills over New Preston Falls.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 109, Washington
members.blurb: Three miles of Route 109 in the hill town of Washington, running east from its short overlap with Route 47 toward Morris, a country road added to the state's scenic list in 2017.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Litchfield
members.blurb: Four state roads meet at Litchfield's green, a 1720 common pasture turned park at the heart of a landmark district of Georgian clapboard houses, and each stays scenic for a few miles out of town.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Harwinton
members.blurb: A mile and a half of Route 4 through Harwinton center, where Litchfield Road comes in from the west on the line of the Litchfield and Harwinton Turnpike, chartered in 1798.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Farmington River to Collinsville
members.blurb: Route 4 and Route 179 follow the Farmington River upstream into Collinsville, a mill village whose axe-factory buildings, closed since 1966, still ramble along the riverbank among old sluices.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 69, Burlington
members.blurb: Three miles of Route 69 in Burlington, on the northern tail of a highway that begins in New Haven, here narrowed to a secondary road running up toward Burlington center and Route 4.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 10, Farmington
members.blurb: Just over a mile of Route 10 down Farmington's Main Street, lined with houses older than 1835 and passing the 1771 First Church and a brick hotel built about 1830 for Farmington Canal travelers.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Barkhamsted Reservoir roads
members.blurb: From Pleasant Valley the road crosses the West Branch of the Farmington, runs along the top of Saville Dam, a stone-trimmed 1940 embankment holding Hartford's water, and follows the shore of Lake McDonough.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US 202, New Hartford
members.blurb: Five miles of US 202 across southern New Hartford toward the Canton line, crossing the Nepaug River where it slides into the Nepaug Reservoir, one of the Metropolitan District Commission's water-supply lakes.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Colebrook
members.blurb: Route 183 runs through Colebrook center, a village in an isolated valley that has changed little since 1860, with a Greek Revival church of 1842 at the foot of its triangular common, and on to North Colebrook.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 272, Norfolk
members.blurb: Route 272 crosses the hill town of Norfolk to the Massachusetts line, by the triangular green of a former railroad-era summer resort and the foot of the drive up Haystack Mountain to a 1929 stone lookout tower.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Roxbury
members.blurb: Nearly four miles of Route 67 through Roxbury, whose Mine Hill quarries sent granite to the Brooklyn Bridge, with a short spur of Route 317 up Church Street past the Congregational church.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 33, Wilton
members.blurb: Ridgefield Road leaves Wilton center, where the 1790 Congregational church is the oldest church building in Fairfield County, and runs nearly five miles northwest to the Ridgefield line.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 53, Redding
members.blurb: Two miles of Route 53 north from the Weston line in Redding, on the old Newtown Turnpike near the Saugatuck Reservoir, whose 1942 dam drowned the villages of Hull and Valley Forge.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 58, Easton
members.blurb: Black Rock Turnpike runs three miles through Easton beside the Hemlock Reservoir, a 1914 water-supply lake for the Bridgeport area, close by the road British troops marched up toward Danbury in April 1777.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 136, Westport
members.blurb: A short run of Route 136 in Westport that begins on the Saugatuck River Bridge, an 1884 wrought-iron swing span turned by hand crank and the oldest surviving movable bridge in Connecticut.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US 1, Madison
members.blurb: Two miles of the Boston Post Road through Madison, past the town green laid out in 1705 and its 1838 Congregational church, facing a row of 18th- and 19th-century houses across the road.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Routes 79 and 80, North Madison
members.blurb: Two miles of Route 80 east from the North Madison roundabout on the line of the 1824 Fairhaven Turnpike, ending at the Hammonasset River and a 1934 open-spandrel arch bridge at the Killingworth line.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 146, Branford to Guilford
members.blurb: Route 146 takes the long way from Branford to the Guilford green, twelve miles by the shore at Indian Neck and Pine Orchard and out Leetes Island Road, ducking under the railroad several times.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 77, Guilford to Durham
members.blurb: Route 77 runs fourteen miles inland from the Guilford green on the 1824 Guilford and Durham Turnpike, past Lake Quonnipaug, then joins Route 17 into Durham, an old farming town with New England's largest volunteer fair.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: US 1, Old Lyme
members.blurb: Just under a mile of the Post Road in Old Lyme, crossing the Lieutenant River beside the Florence Griswold house, where painters of the Old Lyme Art Colony boarded while shaping American Impressionism.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 154, Old Saybrook and Fenwick
members.blurb: Route 154 loops six miles around Old Saybrook's shore, across the causeway over South Cove to Fenwick, a Shingle-style summer borough at the mouth of the Connecticut River with two lighthouses off Lynde Point.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 154, Haddam
members.blurb: Route 154 follows the west bank of the Connecticut River for nine miles through Haddam on the line of the Middlesex Turnpike, a toll road from 1802 to 1876, passing the riverside meadows of Haddam Meadows State Park.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: East Haddam Bridge and Route 149
members.blurb: Route 82 crosses the Connecticut on a steel swing bridge of 1913 and lands beside the Goodspeed Opera House, where Annie began, and Route 149 then turns north along the river through East Haddam's historic district.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lyme: Hadlyme ferry road and Hamburg
members.blurb: Off the Selden III, the little ferry that has crossed here since 1769, Route 148 runs into Hadlyme below Gillette Castle, and Route 156 runs south through Hamburg, the village center of Lyme.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 151, Middle Haddam
members.blurb: A mile and a half of Middle Haddam Road on the east bank of the Connecticut, through the village of Middle Haddam, a river port from about 1730 to 1880 whose shipyards launched ocean-going vessels.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 160, Glastonbury ferry road
members.blurb: A mile of Route 160 inland from the Glastonbury landing of the Rocky Hill ferry, in service since 1655, across the Great Meadows, where the fields still follow seventeenth-century patterns, to Roaring Brook.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Windham Center and Scotland
members.blurb: Route 203 crosses the Shetucket to Windham Center's green, once a county seat, and Route 14 heads east into Scotland past the saltbox where Samuel Huntington, a signer of the Declaration of Independence, was born.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 97, Abington to Pomfret Center
members.blurb: Route 97 leaves the village of Abington, where a 1751 meetinghouse is the oldest church building in Connecticut still in use, and runs four and a half miles north to Pomfret Center.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 244, Pomfret
members.blurb: Three miles of Route 244 into Pomfret Center on the old Boston Turnpike, a toll road chartered in 1797 that was one of the principal ways from Hartford to Boston.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 164, Preston City
members.blurb: Route 164 runs north out of Preston City, a crossroads village of Federal and Greek Revival houses built when Preston farms fed the port of Norwich, for nearly three miles to the Griswold line.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 27, Old Mystic
members.blurb: Under a mile of Route 27 up the east bank of the Mystic River, with the water in view much of the way, ending on Main Street in the village of Old Mystic.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 234, Pequot Trail
members.blurb: Three miles of the Pequot Trail, an old cross-country road through Stonington from Old Mystic toward Pawcatuck that the state numbered, handed back to the town and took over again between 1932 and 1963.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 207, Hebron to Sprague
members.blurb: Route 207, the newest scenic road on the state list, runs sixteen miles east from Hebron past Lebanon's mile-long green, a rare surviving colonial common with its Revolutionary War Office, to the Shetucket River at Baltic.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Tolland Green
members.blurb: Route 74, the Tolland Stage Road, cuts straight across Tolland's long, narrow green, past the 1822 county courthouse and the old county jail that is now a museum.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Route 75, Suffield
members.blurb: Route 75 runs up Suffield's Main Street and on to the Massachusetts line, through a historic district of houses built as tobacco brought the town its fortune and past Suffield Academy, founded in 1833.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).
